explanation: The result composes two proved steps from the source. The first turns the uniform power-law hypothesis into successive approximants whose logarithmic weights beat an arbitrary history-dependent selector. The second chooses the selector to enforce the $X$ margin and strict $D$-weighted product growth while preserving the approximation data. Its role in the campaign is the normalized approximation-sequence constructor used by later admissible-parameter and determinant estimates.
natural_language_statement:
Let $\nu,X,D\in\mathbb R$ with $\nu>0$. Assume the conditional hypothesis $h_{\mathrm{bad}}$: for every $Q\in\mathbb N$ there are $p\in\mathbb Z$ and $q\in\mathbb N$ with $Q\le q$ and $$\left|\pi-\frac{p}{q}\right|\le q^{-\nu}. $$

Then there are sequences $p_n,q_n,x_n$ with $x_0=1$, $x_{n+1}=\lceil\log q_n\rceil$, the same approximation bound, $q_n\ge2$, $p_n\ne0$, $1\le\lceil\log q_n\rceil$, $X<x_{n+1}$, and

$$D\prod_{j<i}x_j<x_i\qquad(i>0).$$

This is conditional on $h_{\mathrm{bad}}$ and $\nu>0$; it does not assert that the hypothesis holds unconditionally for $\pi$.

source_witness.mathematical_role: Composition node: converts the conditional unbounded-denominator approximation input into the normalized sequence and multiplicative growth package consumed downstream.

theorem_title: Normalized successive rational approximations from a uniform power-law hypothesis
